page: Microsoft Azure M176bds_v3 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Intel Xeon 8473C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 176 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 88 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It operates at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of RAM, yielding approximately 8.73 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided via a 410 GB SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The hardware excels in memory bandwidth, achieving 432.14 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 186.33 GB/sec for uncached large-block writes. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top tier, with Redis reaching 170.86 million operations per second. Single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and bzip3 single-threaded decompression falling into the average category.

Given its massive memory capacity and high vCPU count, this instance offers high resource density suitable for large-scale enterprise workloads. The qualitative cost-to-performance ratio is highly favorable for multi-threaded, memory-intensive applications that can leverage the Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets. It is highly suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
